thread.title: Baylor men's golf finishes 10th at Mountaineer Invitational
thread.title_full: Baylor men's golf finishes 10th at Mountaineer Invitational

author: h. k. mckee
title: Baylor men's golf finishes 10th at Mountaineer Invitational
text:
The Baylor men’s golf team finished in 10th place at the Mountaineer Invitational, held at Pete Dye Golf Club, according to an April 14 announcement. Junior Davis Ovard helped lead the team by shooting a 1-under-par 71 in the final round, one of only two sub-par rounds for Baylor during the week.
The result placed Baylor in the middle of a competitive field, with a total score of 21-over-par 885 across three rounds. The Bears were just three shots behind eighth place out of nineteen teams. Clemson claimed the team title with a score of 20-under-par (844), narrowly beating Texas Tech, which finished at 18-under (846). Host West Virginia secured third place at 16-under (848), while TCU and Oklahoma State tied for fourth with scores of nine under par (855).
Interim head coach Ryan Murphy said, “Pete Dye Golf Club was a terrific golf course and test . . . extremely challenging. We had some nice rounds this week, although our finish was not what we had in mind. We will get some rest once back in Waco, and then our preparation for Prairie Dunes will begin.” Murphy also praised individual performances: “Very solid golf from Alex again this week. Proud of his effort,” he said about UConn transfer Alex Heard’s fifth top-25 finish after placing twenty-fifth overall. He added, “Also happy with Davis’s final two rounds after a slow start. And Jonas and Evan contributed some nice rounds as well.” Senior Sam Dossey rebounded from an opening-round setback to tie for ninety-first.
Oklahoma State’s Preston Stout won medalist honors by finishing eleven under par (205), edging out Clemson’s Thomas Higgins by one stroke.
With the regular season now complete, Baylor will next compete in the Big 12 Championship scheduled for April 27-29 at Prairie Dunes Country Club in Hutchinson, Kansas.
